summary: This room turned out to be two worlds sharing a folder-blind topology slot: the palace's three foundational meta docs (CLAUDE.md, ELDER.md, SCHEMA — Reference.md) and five Shop visualization/typesetting Specialists (D3.js, LaTeX, Matplotlib, Mermaid, Observable Plot). The Shop entries are internally tight — already cross-linked via alternative-to/enables/fallback-for and all member-of The Shop — so the real work here was the meta side, which is thick with wikilinks written in body prose that never made it into frontmatter `links:`. Four of those unlinked mentions happen to point straight at this Weave's priority newcomers (Agent Toolbox, Making a Palace Citizen, Return Ceremony, The Palace Voice), so promoting them is close to free inbound-wiring. The more interesting cross-domain thread is a genuine but unglamorous pattern: three Specialists (LaTeX, Matplotlib, Mermaid) carry an open question about building a house design-system wrapper and defer it "to first job," while two siblings (D3.js, Observable Plot) already built and shipped that exact wrapper (`palace-tokens.js` additive pattern; `palace-plot-defaults.js` subtractive pattern) — the answer to the open question already exists two entries over, it just isn't named or pointed at. No merge/compost/demote candidates surfaced; every entry in the room earns its keep and destroying any of them would lose a distinct charter, so on the "cluttered" concern this room reports clean.

coherence_findings.issue: Structural echo, not a genuine link to force: every Shop Specialist's Job Contract Output section says out_path is "an absolute path under the target entry's bundle" — that is SCHEMA — Reference §8's Entry Bundles rule, applied verbatim five times, but no Specialist actually links to SCHEMA — Reference and none should be made to (the relationship is generic infrastructure, true of nearly every palace entry, not a distinguishing finding for this room).
coherence_findings.proposed_action: none — noting only so a future pass doesn't rediscover it as a false surprise

open_question_resolutions.question: A palace.sty shared preamble (fontspec stack, six-skin xcolor, microtype defaults) — deferred to first real job.
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: The design pattern to copy already exists and is documented: Observable Plot's palace-plot-defaults.js (subtractive wrapper, overrides strong tool defaults once) and D3.js's palace-tokens.js (additive, read-at-call-time). LaTeX's palace.sty is the same shape of problem — point the eventual author at those two files as the precedent before it's designed from scratch. Still genuinely gated on LaTeX's first real job landing, so leave the open question open but add the pointer.

open_question_resolutions.question: Default palace.mplstyle style sheet — deferred to first real job.
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Same precedent as LaTeX above — palace-plot-defaults.js / palace-tokens.js are the worked examples of additive-vs-subtractive house wrappers; Matplotlib's own Forward Vector already names wanting "a palace.mplstyle house wrapper... the way Plot's wrapper already does," so the entry itself half-sees this — just missing the explicit pointer.

open_question_resolutions.question: Should the Shop maintain a base themeVariables object for the palace palette — deferred to first real job.
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Same precedent again. Mermaid's forward_vector already names hungering for "the missing --cssFile house wrapper" — add the explicit pointer to the two solved cases so the pattern isn't reinvented.

synthesis_spawn_flag.unnamed_idea: The house-defaults wrapper pattern — an additive vs. subtractive design for bridging a tool's own defaults to the Loudon Live design-system tokens (colors_and_type.css / palace-tokens.js), read at call time so a live skin swap propagates. Currently instantiated twice (D3.js's additive palette read, Observable Plot's palacePlot() subtractive override) and named as an open, deferred want in three siblings (LaTeX's palace.sty, Matplotlib's palace.mplstyle, Mermaid's --cssFile).
synthesis_spawn_flag.why_load_bearing: It recurs identically across every Specialist in this room's Shop half, in two solved and three unsolved instances, yet has no entry of its own to hold the general shape (additive vs. subtractive, load-order rules, token-at-call-time discipline). Right now the pattern only exists duplicated across five bodies of prose, so the next Specialist to face this problem is likely to reinvent it instead of reading it.
